title: Contract formation versus selection of terms
shortTitle: Contract formation versus selection of terms
summary: Whether a contract exists and whether a disputed term belongs to it are separate questions.
notes: Under § 2-207(1), an expression of acceptance can form a contract despite differences; subsection (2) then addresses additional terms. If the writings fail but the parties perform, subsection (3) supplies a different formation-and-terms route. Hill and Klocek disagree at an earlier stage about whether the transaction was already formed when the terms arrived. The classification of the sequence often determines the next test.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 274–304. Open assigned page 274.
